correctness.rationale: The source graph formula has two branches g+ g- with g+g-=-1 and weights alpha=1/(1+y^-2). Their weights sum to one, proving the first marginal. Differentiating J(g)=-phi(t) cancels weights in the pushforward Jacobian and yields pi sum_{phi(t)=s}1/phi prime(t), s=-J(y). Vieta and differentiation give 1/a for a>0 and Gamma/(b-s)^2 for a=0. Roots at b+J=0 are two simple nonzero y values; quadratic blow-up is not locally integrable but gives no atoms. Comparison of rational densities and graph intersections proves both equivalence and mutual singularity.

value.rationale: The pair of coordinate marginals is the natural invariant for a two-variable measure; the sharp finite-vs-infinite local-mass transition and continuum many mutually singular extremal measures sharing both marginals show that even complete marginal data fail to identify the extremal joint measure. This is a substantive structural finding, beyond reusing the source graph representation.
